Lindley, A.A. (1997). An Economic and Environmental Analysis of the Chlor-Alkali Production Process: Mercury Cells and Alternative Technologies. Final Report, 30 June 1997, prepared for the European Commission (DG III C-4, Chemicals, plastics, rubber), Brussels. Author on secondment from ICI Chemicals & Polymers.

Loaded: electrolysis electricity and caustic-evaporation steam (MWh/t chlorine) for mercury, diaphragm and membrane cells (Sect. 5.3 table, from SRIC 1997/Euro Chlor 1994); new-installation membrane electricity at 5 and 3 kA/m2; minimum load; cell-room lifetime; mercury-to-membrane conversion capex (typical 560-610, ideal 360, 1990 case 408 ECU/t capacity, SRIC 700 USD/t) as incremental; grass-roots membrane plant 870 ECU/t capacity as total-plant; air-cathode (oxygen-depolarized) cell description. Not loaded: mercury emissions/limits (non-GHG), trade and capacity statistics, aggregate EU phase-out costs. Other-values: cost shares, cost changes after conversion, indirect CO2 per t chlorine by power source. Locator: printed page numbers (roman i-iii for the executive summary, arabic thereafter). Traps: no price year anywhere (1997 used); ECU recorded as EUR; steam given in MWh/t with no heating-value basis; all energy per t chlorine (1 EChemU = 1 t Cl2 + 1.1 t NaOH + H2); 408 ECU/t is a 1990 cost at 1997 exchange rate.
